wiki.extract: The Statue of Liberty is a colossal neoclassical sculpture of a robed and crowned woman on Liberty Island, part of New York City, in New York Harbor. The copper-clad statue, a gift to the United States from the people of France, was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, and its metal framework built by Gustave Eiffel. The statue was dedicated on October 28, 1886.

Grand Canyon National Park is a national park of the United States located in northwestern Arizona, the 15th site to have been named as a national park. The park's central feature is the Grand Canyon, a gorge of the Colorado River, which is often considered one of the Wonders of the World. The park, which covers 1,217,262 acres of unincorporated area in Coconino and Mohave counties, received more than 4.9 million recreational visitors in 2024. The Grand Canyon was designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1979. The park celebrated its 100th anniversary on February 26, 2019.

White Americans are Americans who identify as white people. In a more official sense, the United States Census Bureau, which collects demographic data on Americans, defines "white" as "[a] person having origins in any of the original peoples of Europe, the Middle East, or North Africa". White Americans have historically constituted the majority population in the United States, though their share has been gradually declining in recent decades. As of the latest American Community Survey conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau in 2024, an estimated 59.8% of the U.S. population—approximately 203.3 million people—identify as White alone, while Non-Hispanic Whites account for 56.3% of the population, or roughly 191.4 million people. Overall, 72.1% of Americans identify as White either alone or in combination with one or more other racial groups. European Americans are by far the largest panethnic group of White Americans and have constituted the majority population of the United States since the nation's founding. Middle Eastern Americans constitute a much smaller demographic of White Americans, making up around 1.1% of the US population in 2020.

The Mount Rushmore National Memorial is a national memorial featuring a colossal sculpture carved into the granite face of Mount Rushmore in the Black Hills, about 2 mi (3 km) southwest of Keystone, South Dakota, United States. The sculptor, Gutzon Borglum, named it the Shrine of Democracy, and oversaw the execution from 1927 to 1941 with the help of his son, Lincoln Borglum. The sculpture features 60-foot-tall (18 m) depictions of the heads of four United States presidents: George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln, respectively chosen to represent the nation's foundation, expansion, development, and preservation. Mount Rushmore attracts more than two million visitors annually to the memorial park which covers 1,278 acres.

The Golden Gate Bridge is a suspension bridge spanning the Golden Gate, the one-mile-wide (1.6 km) strait connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean in California, United States. The structure links San Francisco—the northern tip of the San Francisco Peninsula—to Marin County, carrying both U.S. Route 101 and California State Route 1 across the strait. It also carries pedestrian and bicycle traffic, and is designated as part of U.S. Bicycle Route 95. Recognized by the American Society of Civil Engineers as one of the Wonders of the Modern World, the bridge is one of the most internationally recognized symbols of San Francisco and California.

Thanksgiving or Thanksgiving Day is a national holiday celebrated on various dates in October and November in the United States, Canada, Saint Lucia, and Liberia. It is also observed in the Australian territory of Norfolk Island. It began as a day of giving thanks for the blessings of the harvest and of the preceding year. Various similarly named harvest festival holidays occur throughout the world during autumn. Although Thanksgiving has historical roots in religious and cultural traditions, it has long been celebrated as a secular holiday as well.

Independence Day is celebrated annually on 15 August as a public holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the United Kingdom on 15 August 1947. On this day the Indian Independence Act 1947 came into effect, transferring legislative sovereignty to the Indian Constituent Assembly. India attained independence following the independence movement noted for largely non-violent resistance and civil disobedience led by the Indian National Congress under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi.

The Super Bowl is the league championship final game of the National Football League (NFL) of the United States. It has served as the final game of every NFL season since 1966 replacing the NFL Championship Game and also served as the final game of every American Football League season from 1966 to 1967 prior to the AFL–NFL merger replacing the AFL championship game. Since 2022, the game has been played on the second Sunday in February. Prior Super Bowls were played on Sundays in early to mid-January from 1967 to 1978, late January from 1979 to 2003, and the first Sunday of February from 2004 to 2021. Winning teams are awarded the Vince Lombardi Trophy, named after the coach who won the first two Super Bowls. Because the NFL restricts the use of its "Super Bowl" trademark, it is frequently referred to as the "big game" or other generic terms by non-sponsoring corporations. The day the game is held is commonly referred to as "Super Bowl Sunday" or "Super Sunday".

Mardi Gras, also known as Shrove Tuesday, is the final day of Carnival ; it thus falls on the day before the beginning of Lent on Ash Wednesday. Mardi Gras is French for "Fat Tuesday", referring to it being the last day of consuming rich, fatty foods, most notably red meat, in preparation for the Christian fasting season of Lent, during which such foods are avoided.

Halloween, also known as All Hallows' Eve, or All Saints' Eve, is a celebration observed in many countries on 31 October, the eve of the Western Christian feast of All Hallows' Day. It is at the beginning of the observance of Allhallowtide, the time in the Christian liturgical year dedicated to remembering the dead, including saints (hallows), martyrs, and all the faithful departed. In popular culture, Halloween has become a celebration of horror and is associated with the macabre and the supernatural.

food_writeup: American cuisine is diverse, influenced by various immigrant cultures, featuring iconic foods like hamburgers, hot dogs, barbecue, and regional specialties such as New England clam chowder and Southern fried chicken.
brief_history: Founded in 1776 after declaring independence from Britain, the USA expanded westward, became a global power through industrialization and world wars, and remains a major political, economic, and cultural influence worldwide.
current_conflicts: The USA is involved in various international diplomatic and military engagements, including counterterrorism efforts and geopolitical tensions, but no large-scale active wars on its own soil.

main_events.headline: Democrats retake Congress
main_events.summary: November midterms punish Bush over Iraq; defense secretary Rumsfeld resigns after heavy losses.

main_events.headline: Iraq violence spirals
main_events.summary: Sectarian bloodshed peaks in Baghdad; mounting US casualties deepen public opposition and political pressure.

sport.headline: Steelers win Super Bowl XL
sport.summary: Pittsburgh beats Seattle in Detroit in February for the franchise's fifth Super Bowl title.

main_events.headline: Bush orders Iraq troop surge
main_events.summary: An extra 20,000 troops deploy in January; sectarian violence gradually falls by year-end under Petraeus' strategy.

main_events.headline: Subprime mortgage crisis erupts
main_events.summary: Housing defaults spread through summer; Bear Stearns funds collapse in August as credit markets freeze.

sport.headline: Patriots complete perfect regular season
sport.summary: New England goes 16-0, the first perfect regular season since the schedule expanded to sixteen games.

main_events.headline: Lehman collapse triggers global crisis
main_events.summary: Lehman Brothers fails in September; credit markets convulse and governments worldwide rush massive bailouts.

main_events.headline: Obama elected president
main_events.summary: November victory over McCain makes Barack Obama the first Black US president, with a decisive Electoral College margin.

sport.headline: Phelps wins eight golds in Beijing
sport.summary: Michael Phelps sweeps all eight swimming events, the most golds ever at one Olympics.

main_events.headline: Stimulus passes; health reform battle begins
main_events.summary: The $787 billion ARRA passes in February; the fight over Obamacare dominates the year.

main_events.headline: Obama surges troops in Afghanistan
main_events.summary: December order sends 30,000 more troops as the Taliban insurgency intensifies across the south and east.

sport.headline: Steelers win Super Bowl XLIII
sport.summary: Pittsburgh edges Arizona in Tampa in February on a last-minute Santonio Holmes touchdown catch.

main_events.headline: Affordable Care Act becomes law
main_events.summary: Landmark health reform passes in March on party-line votes after a bruising fight in Congress.

main_events.headline: Tea Party wave in the midterms
main_events.summary: Republicans retake the House in November amid backlash to Obama and stimulus spending.

sport.headline: Saints win first Super Bowl
sport.summary: New Orleans beats Indianapolis in Miami in February, lifting a city still rebuilding five years after Katrina.

main_events.headline: Bin Laden killed in Pakistan raid
main_events.summary: May SEAL raid in Abbottabad ends the 9/11 mastermind's nearly decade on the run.

main_events.headline: Debt-ceiling crisis rattles markets
main_events.summary: August standoff brings the US near default; S&P strips its AAA credit rating for the first time.

sport.headline: Packers win Super Bowl XLV
sport.summary: Green Bay beats Pittsburgh in Dallas in February for the franchise's fourth title behind Aaron Rodgers' MVP performance.

main_events.headline: Obama wins re-election
main_events.summary: November victory over Romney; Democrats hold the Senate despite a sluggish economy and high unemployment.

main_events.headline: Benghazi attack kills four Americans
main_events.summary: September assault on the US consulate in Libya, including the ambassador, sparks a political firestorm.

sport.headline: US tops the London medal table
sport.summary: Americans win 104 medals with 22 golds; Phelps retires as the most decorated Olympian ever.

main_events.headline: Government shutdown over Obamacare
main_events.summary: A 16-day October shutdown follows a failed GOP bid to defund the health law.

main_events.headline: Snowden exposes NSA surveillance
main_events.summary: June leaks reveal mass data collection; Snowden flees to Russia via Hong Kong, sparking a global privacy debate.

sport.headline: Heat repeat as NBA champions
sport.summary: Miami beats San Antonio in seven games in June; LeBron James earns Finals MVP again.

main_events.headline: US leads sanctions over Crimea
main_events.summary: Washington coordinates Western sanctions after Russia's March annexation of Crimea and backs Kyiv with aid.

main_events.headline: Airstrikes against ISIS begin
main_events.summary: US bombs ISIS targets in Iraq and Syria in August as the group seizes Mosul.

sport.headline: Seahawks win first Super Bowl
sport.summary: Seattle crushes Denver in New York in February; the Legion of Boom defense dominates from kickoff.

main_events.headline: Iran nuclear deal signed
main_events.summary: July JCPOA trades sanctions relief for strict curbs on Iran's nuclear program over the next decade.

main_events.headline: Paris climate accord adopted
main_events.summary: December deal commits the US and nearly 200 nations to emissions cuts in a landmark global pact.

sport.headline: US women win the World Cup
sport.summary: The USWNT beats Japan 5-2 in Vancouver; Lloyd's hat trick seals a third star.

main_events.headline: Trump elected president
main_events.summary: November upset over Clinton upends US politics and rattles global alliances, despite losing the popular vote.

main_events.headline: Russia accused of election interference
main_events.summary: US intelligence blames Moscow for hacks and leaks aimed at the campaign in a January assessment.

sport.headline: Cubs end 108-year drought
sport.summary: Chicago beats Cleveland in seven games for its first World Series since 1908 in a November classic.

main_events.headline: Travel ban sparks protests
main_events.summary: January order restricting entry from several Muslim-majority nations faces court blocks and airport demonstrations nationwide.

main_events.headline: Charlottesville rally turns deadly
main_events.summary: August white-supremacist rally kills a counterprotester; Trump's response draws bipartisan condemnation after he blames both sides.

sport.headline: Patriots' historic Super Bowl comeback
sport.summary: New England erases a 25-point deficit to beat Atlanta in overtime in Houston in February.

main_events.headline: Trade war with China begins
main_events.summary: July tariffs on Chinese goods worth tens of billions open a multi-year conflict roiling global markets.

main_events.headline: Democrats retake the House
main_events.summary: November midterms deliver a check on Trump's power amid record turnout and suburban revolt against the president.

sport.headline: Eagles win first Super Bowl
sport.summary: Philadelphia upsets New England in Minneapolis in February in a high-scoring thriller behind backup quarterback Nick Foles.

main_events.headline: Trump impeached over Ukraine
main_events.summary: December impeachment on abuse-of-power charges for pressuring Kyiv; the Senate acquits him in 2020.

main_events.headline: Phase-one China trade deal
main_events.summary: December truce pauses tariff escalation after 18 months of tensions as both sides claim wins.

sport.headline: USWNT wins World Cup again
sport.summary: The Americans beat the Netherlands in Lyon in July to repeat as world champions before a global audience.

main_events.headline: COVID-19 pandemic ravages the US
main_events.summary: Lockdowns spread in March; hundreds of thousands die as the economy craters, then partially recovers by fall.

main_events.headline: Biden defeats Trump
main_events.summary: November victory ends a bitter campaign as mail-in ballots tip key states; Trump refuses to concede defeat.

sport.headline: Sports shut down, then bubble up
sport.summary: Leagues halt in March; the NBA finishes its season in a Florida bubble, won by the Lakers.

main_events.headline: Capitol riot shocks the nation
main_events.summary: January 6 mob storms Congress in an unprecedented attack as lawmakers certify Biden's election victory.

main_events.headline: Chaotic withdrawal from Afghanistan
main_events.summary: August exit ends 20 years of war as evacuations turn desperate; the Taliban swiftly retakes Kabul.

main_events.headline: Biden's domestic agenda advances
main_events.summary: March stimulus and November infrastructure bill pass on party lines amid inflation worries.

sport.headline: US tops Tokyo's medal table
sport.summary: Americans win 113 medals at the delayed Games in August, edging China in golds.

main_events.headline: US rallies behind Ukraine
main_events.summary: February Russian invasion triggers massive American military aid and sanctions coordinated with European allies, worth tens of billions.

main_events.headline: Dobbs ends federal abortion rights
main_events.summary: June Supreme Court ruling in a 6-3 decision overturns Roe v. Wade, returning the issue to states.

sport.headline: USMNT returns to the World Cup
sport.summary: The Americans reach the round of 16 in Qatar in a young squad's debut before falling to the Netherlands.

main_events.headline: Debt-ceiling standoff resolved
main_events.summary: A June deal between Biden and McCarthy averts a first-ever US default after weeks of brinkmanship.

main_events.headline: US backs Israel after October 7
main_events.summary: Hamas attack triggers American military aid and a regional crisis as the Gaza war begins, drawing protests at home.

sport.headline: Messi mania hits American soccer
sport.summary: Lionel Messi joins Inter Miami in July, transforming MLS's profile overnight and selling out stadiums nationwide.

main_events.headline: Trump wins comeback election
main_events.summary: November victory over Kamala Harris makes him the second president to win non-consecutive terms in a decisive return.

main_events.headline: Biden drops out, Harris steps in
main_events.summary: July withdrawal after a disastrous debate upends the Democratic ticket, making Harris the nominee with 100 days to go.

sport.headline: US shines at the Paris Olympics
sport.summary: Americans top the Paris medal table with 126 medals, most of any nation, led by Biles and Ledecky.

main_events.headline: Trump's second term begins
main_events.summary: January inauguration launches mass deportations and a federal workforce overhaul with sweeping executive orders on day one.

main_events.headline: Liberation Day tariffs shock markets
main_events.summary: Sweeping April tariffs ignite a global trade war and market turmoil, with rates unseen in a century.

sport.headline: Eagles deny Chiefs' three-peat
sport.summary: Philadelphia routs Kansas City in New Orleans in February to win Super Bowl LIX, ending the dynasty bid.
